## Summary of Changes Hello, I'm Gemini Code Assist[^1]! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed! This pull request resolves a critical issue where stale entries in the metadata cache of weed mount instances persisted even after files were deleted on the Filer, leading to data inconsistency. The solution involves a significant refactoring of the metadata cache's directory refresh and entry deletion mechanisms. By implementing atomic directory replacement, enhancing synchronization during batch inserts, and introducing a pending delete journal, the changes ensure that all mount instances accurately reflect the current state of the file system, preventing 'ghost' files from appearing. ### Highlights * **Metadata Cache Refresh Consistency**: Fixed metadata cache refresh consistency by introducing atomic directory replacement, ensuring that stale entries are properly removed. * **Atomic Directory Replacement**: Implemented a new `ReplaceDirectoryEntries` function that atomically clears existing directory cache entries and inserts new ones under a single lock, preventing race conditions. * **Synchronization for Inserts**: Synchronized insert operations in `doEnsureVisited` with a lock to prevent reinsertion of entries that were deleted by subscriber events during a previous cache cycle. * **Pending Delete Journal**: Introduced a `pendingDeletes` journal to track entries deleted between fetching a directory listing and atomically replacing entries, filtering them out to prevent reinsertion. * **Local Delete Event Processing**: Modified the `Unlink` operation to allow local delete events to be processed by the mount subscriber, ensuring consistency across instances. 🧠 **New Feature in Public Preview:** You can now enable **Memory** to help **Gemini Code Assist** learn from your team's feedback. This makes future code reviews more consistent and personalized to your project's style. **Click [here](https://codeassist.google/code-review/login) to enable Memory in your admin console.**
Changelog * **weed/mount/meta_cache/meta_cache.go** * Introduced a `pendingDeletes` map to track entries marked for deletion during a directory refresh. * Added `ReplaceDirectoryEntries` function for atomically clearing and inserting directory entries. * Implemented `BeginRefresh`, `CancelRefresh`, and `recordPendingDelete` methods to manage the pending delete journal. * Integrated `recordPendingDelete` calls into `AtomicUpdateEntryFromFiler` and `DeleteEntry` to mark items for filtering. * **weed/mount/meta_cache/meta_cache_init.go** * Refactored `doEnsureVisited` to collect all directory entries first, then use `ReplaceDirectoryEntries` for atomic updates. * Removed incremental batch insertion logic in favor of the new atomic replacement mechanism. * Integrated `BeginRefresh` and `CancelRefresh` calls to manage the pending delete state during directory refreshes. * **weed/mount/weedfs.go** * Added calls to `metaCache.BeginRefresh` before and `metaCache.CancelRefresh` on error during the `EnsureVisited` call to properly manage the refresh state. * **weed/mount/weedfs_file_mkrm.go** * Modified the `filer_pb.Remove` call in the `Unlink` function to pass an empty `signatures` array, ensuring local delete events are processed by the mount subscriber and not filtered out.
Activity * No specific activity (comments, reviews, etc.) has been recorded for this pull request.
Using Gemini Code Assist
The full guide for Gemini Code Assist can be found on our [documentation page](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-github-code), here are some quick tips. Invoking Gemini You can request assistance from Gemini at any point by creating a comment using either `/gemini ` or `@gemini-code-assist `. Below is a summary of the supported commands on the current page. Feature | Command | Description --- | --- | --- Code Review | `/gemini review` | Performs a code review for the current pull request in its current state. Pull Request Summary | `/gemini summary` | Provides a summary of the current pull request in its current state. Comment | @gemini-code-assist | Responds in comments when explicitly tagged, both in pull request comments and review comments. Help | `/gemini help` | Displays a list of available commands. Customization To customize Gemini Code Assist for GitHub experience, repository maintainers can create a configuration file and/or provide a custom code review style guide (such as PEP-8 for Python) by creating and adding files to a `.gemini/` folder in the base of the repository. Detailed instructions can be found [here](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/customize-gemini-behavior-github). Limitations & Feedback Gemini Code Assist may make mistakes. Please leave feedback on any instances where its feedback is incorrect or counter productive. You can react with :thumbsup: and :thumbsdown: on @gemini-code-assist comments. If you're interested in giving your feedback about your experience with Gemini Code Assist for Github and other Google products, sign up [here](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2cyuGuTWsEw84yG). You can also get AI-powered code generation, chat, as well as code reviews directly in the IDE at no cost with the [Gemini Code Assist IDE Extension](https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini/code-assist).

body:
thanks a lot for the fix! 

I was thinking there could be some metadata updates missed when fuse mount receives from the filer.

This particular fix seems specific for deletions, which may not reveal the actual problem.

Not sure. Need some effort to debug.

Yes, this fix only addresses the bug where **deletions can be semi-permanently missed in the metadata cache**. In our use case, **large batch deletions are frequent**, and we observed a persistent state where deletions appeared **inconsistently across nodes** (some nodes showing files as deleted while others still showed them). This caused service issues, so we reported and fixed it urgently. In tests, the issue reproduced **very frequently**, leaving **dozens to hundreds of entries** each time. After adding detailed logs and analyzing **10,000 create/delete operations**, I found that even when **all filer subscription events were delivered**, deleted entries could still reappear in the metadata cache for two reasons: * **Directory cache refresh performs inserts without corresponding deletes**, so if a cache delete is missed once (e.g., due to a network error), stale entries may remain indefinitely. * **There is no synchronization between cache inserts and deletes triggered by `Unlink`**, so a deleted entry can be reinserted into the metadata cache. * LevelDB writes are thread-safe, but the **operation order is non-deterministic**, so synchronization is needed. If there is an **event loss issue**, it likely requires separate debugging. However, even without event loss, the bug where **deleted entries can reappear in the metadata cache** still needs to be addressed. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant U as FUSE Unlink(Y) participant MC as MetaCache (LevelDB) participant F as Filer participant E as doEnsureVisited participant S as Subscription Handler Note over S,E: Deletion on Host2 → 64+ subscription events/2s
→ RecordDirectoryUpdate → maybeRefreshDirectory Note over E: InvalidateChildrenCache(dir) E->>F: ReadDirAllEntries(dir) start Note over F: Y exists at the iterator snapshot point Note over U: Host1 requests deletion of file Y U->>F: filer_pb.Remove(Y, sig=[Host1]) F-->>U: OK (Y deletion completed in filer) U->>MC: DeleteEntry(Y) [🔒 acquire] Note over MC: Y not inserted yet → no-op ⚠️ U-->>MC: [🔓 release] F-->>E: [..., Y, ...] streaming response E->>MC: doBatchInsertEntries([...Y...]) Note over MC: ⛔ lock not held!
→ Y gets inserted (ghost) E->>MC: markCachedFn(dir) Note over S: Y deletion event received S->>S: sig == selfSignature → return nil Note over S: ❌ Entire event ignored Note over MC: ❌ Y = permanent ghost entry
No reconciliation path ```
